'''David John Richardson''' (born 1964) is a British optoelectronics researcher and [[fellow]] of both the [[Royal Society]] (FRS) and the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]] (FREng).<ref name="royalSocietyRichardson">{{cite web
 |url         = https://royalsociety.org/people/david-richardson-13837/
 |title       = David Richardson
 |website     = The Royal Society
 |publisher   = royalsociety.org
}}</ref> He is currently a '''Partner Researcher at [[Microsoft]]''',<ref>https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/project/craft/people/</ref> based in Romsey, UK, where he leads research on '''hollow core optical fiber''' technology—an approach that guides light through an air-filled core rather than conventional solid glass. Before joining Microsoft, he spent 34 years at the Optoelectronics Research Centre (ORC) at the [[University of Southampton]].<ref>https://www.orc.soton.ac.uk/news/7104</ref> While at the ORC, he served as Professor, Deputy Director, and Head of the Fibre and Laser Group, making significant contributions to advanced optical fibre and laser research.<ref name=soton>{{cite web|url=https://www.orc.soton.ac.uk/people/djr1|title=Professor David Richardson - Optoelectronics Research Centre - University of Southampton|website=www.orc.soton.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name="RichardsonNilsson2010">{{cite journal|last1=Richardson|first1=D. J.|last2=Nilsson|first2=J.|last3=Clarkson|first3=W. A.|title=High power fiber lasers: current status and future perspectives [Invited]|journal=Journal of the Optical Society of America B|volume=27|issue=11|year=2010|pages=B63|issn=0740-3224|doi=10.1364/JOSAB.27.000B63|bibcode=2010JOSAB..27B..63R }} {{closed access}}</ref>

==Education==
Richardson was educated at St George’s [[Catholic School|Roman Catholic School]], [[Southampton]] and [[Richard Taunton Sixth Form College|Taunton’s College]].<ref name=whoswho/> He completed his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree and [[PhD]] in Physics at the [[University of Sussex]] in 1989.<ref name=djphd/>

==Career and research==
Richardson is a pioneer in the field of [[photonics]], best known for his work on [[fibre optic]]s and their applications.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/david-richardson-13837/|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2018|title=Professor David Richardson FREng FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref> He has played a leading role in developing techniques to scale the data-carrying capacity of future [[optical communication]] networks to keep up with society's demand for ever increasing [[Bandwidth (computing)|internet bandwidth]].<ref name=frs/> He has developed [[optical fibre]]s of high performance – capable, for example, of transmitting large quantities of data across the internet at high speed.<ref name=frs/>

Richardson was also one of the first to demonstrate the potential of compact, flexible, pulsed fibre lasers operating over a broad range of powers, pulse durations and wavelengths.<ref name=frs/> Over many years he has extended the performance limits of fibre lasers, making them strong contenders to conventional lasers and contributing to their commercial success.<ref name=frs/> His work extends to fibres capable of delivering [[kilowatt]]s of optical power for manufacturing with lasers.<ref name=frs/>
